selection_status: Established-only scientific vocabulary; upstream definitions and synonyms; unresolved mappings retained.
research_question: How do soil nutrients and microbial or pathogen interactions relate to potato growth, nutrition and plant health?
scope_description: Extract direct source-stated relationships among: (1) nutrient chemicals, supply, soil chemistry and availability; (2) potato root, leaf and tuber structures and potato species identity; (3) root development, root-system form and measured plant/root traits; (4) nutrient uptake and transport at plant or organ level; (5) nutritional composition of potato tissues; (6) microbial organisms, inoculation treatments and pathogens affecting potato nutrition, growth, tissues or plant health. Both endpoints must fit these families with source-established potato or upstream soil-nutrient relevance. Preserve actual species, cultivar, strain, conditions, measurements, aggregation, modality and study applicability. Select independent eligible links in mixed passages. Use full contextual meaning, including explicit abbreviations and antecedents. An eligible missing term remains unresolved, not outside scope. Keep organisms, inoculation events and disease responses distinct; broader classes do not erase cultivar or strain identity. Scope is domain membership, separate from truth or mapping certainty.

selection_history.note: Expand established classes for coverage within the existing potato nutrition scope. Object/data properties, research question, scope and identity rules unchanged. Ontology labels and definitions checked against frozen source RDF; expert mapping review is not claimed.

First core potato nutrient-grounding experiment. Preserve source fragments and prior runs. Defer microbial identities, inoculation and detailed gene/protein/enzyme mechanisms; retain core root development, root hair and generic phosphate/potassium transport. Relations, data properties and identity/merging rules are unchanged. Fresh extraction is required to evaluate the narrower scope.
Restore potato microbial/pathogen scope with six established classes, including PECO plant exposures; relations unchanged.

Verified definitions and identifiers for recurring plant traits and nutrient exposures; distinguish amount/concentration, length/mass ratios, exposure/deficiency and process/material subjects. No exact phosphorus-efficiency concept is invented.

Replaced custom application-schema classes with 204 established OBO Foundry classes imported as verified RDF/OWL fragments from Ontobee (PO, TO, GO, CHEBI, ENVO, PECO, PATO, NCBITaxon, PCO) with full ancestor hierarchies, definitions, and exact/related synonyms.
